utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Let's have Prosecution tab 9, which is 5037. This also is under seal so it should not be broadcast.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And this is a Telex that I'm sure you're familiar with I understand from Cunningham or at least prepared by Cunningham. And on page 2 there is a description of the -- what is described as the JNA scenario and then there are six points. Now, I just want to move you, if I may, to the very last paragraph. "Another defence of the JNA was that they could not be held responsible for the behaviour of the Chetniks. The monitor team is, however, convinced that the JNA very closely co-operated with those reservists and is of the opinion that the leadership of the JNA should directly or indirectly be held responsible for their acts." Now, is it correct that the irregular forces, as far as you could observe them, were acting in close co-operation with the JNA, as described here?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: First allow me a remark, I am not quite sure that this report or fax has been done by Cunningham. I believe that it's a part or the full special report which has been done by the -- our headquarters by some special team of lawyers. So it is -- it has -- it is not originally from regional centre Belgrade. It is done by -- on an investigation which has been done on all territories mission was active. So it is what I do know about this document, but we can check it thoroughly --

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Well, let me just stop you there for one moment. Does that investigation include reliance on the various ECMM reports that you prepared and that other teams prepared?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. And based on your observation, just to come back to my question, do you agree with that last paragraph? Is it true that the JNA very closely co-operated with those reservists?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: This is how I personally perceived that. This is written by military persons who were in the mission as well present, so they have better sense for that. But what I felt is reservists, they have sometimes even tanks, T-34 from the World War II. It's not easy for private person to have it, to support it with grenades and so on. So -- and I do believe that JNA was superior and -- on one hand. On the other hand, in Yugoslavia everywhere there were some hands hidden and people were angry. So local clashes are quite -- I don't want to dare to say "normal," but it could happen. So local armed units can appear by the way we have mentioned Berak, for instance, so the --

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Well, sir, we'll get to Berak.

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: We'll get to Berak. But am I right in respect of Ilok that the only institutional authority on the Serb side with whom you had contact was the JNA?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: No. On the road I have met or we have met -- on the road to Ilok we have met with a group of volunteers what was very visible because of different uniformed -- mixed uniforms and -- okay, we passed through.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Well, when I say "institutional authority," I mean an authority presenting itself as an organised institutional force purporting to exercise jurisdiction over the area. And would you agree that that was, in terms of who you had contact with, only the JNA on the Serb side?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Now, I'd like to ask you some questions about Vukovar, and if I may, I would like to have you take a look at your notebook.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And, Mr. President, since I plan to refer to this notebook quite a number of times, I would like -- I prepared copies for the Judges.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Now, sir, am I correct in understanding - and this appears to be the case from your notebook - that on the 18th of November, your itinerary was starting in Belgrade, passing through the Serbian town of Adasevci, then going to Negoslavci, where you visited the OG South headquarters of the JNA. And then you went, as I understand it, to Vukovar insofar as you were able to visit it and you did go to the Velepromet centre. Is that itinerary correct?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: I believe so. If it is written there in this form, yes, it is. What -- I remember that, yes, we have been in Negoslavci; yes, we have been in Velepromet; and, yes, we have been in Vukovar, not in the down-town but up on the hills, because there is a down-town of Vukovar near the Danube which is down --

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And that's fine, thank you. I just wanted the general itinerary. And do I understand correctly - and this is a question I think you can answer yes or no - that your morning started with a briefing by General Maksimovic of the JNA?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: If it is written, then it is granted.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Well, maybe you should -- do you have your notebook in front of you?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: Yes, I do have this.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Now, if we go over to page 3 of your handwritten version, which is page 2 of the typewritten version - and I apologise for this - there's a heading there and in the handwritten version it's very clear, you have a big heading: "Veselin Sljivancanin."

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Now, am I right in understanding that that page in the handwritten version as well as the next, one, two, three pages, all that information - and this is the pages 7761 to 7764 - all of that concerns information that was given to you by Major Sljivancanin?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: I don't think so, sir. I cannot guarantee that because the name Major Sljivancanin is written there by the other hand -- it's typical Serbian version of the handwriting. And probably he came here, sit to the table, sat to the table, and I gave my notebook to somebody to write who is coming. So this is the name, but definitely I cannot confirm who is the main person for negotiation.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Well, there's a notation on page 04687764 about Velepromet. Can I just ask you, do you recall whether Major Sljivancanin was talking to you about the Velepromet centre?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: I don't remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Was General Maksimovic talking to you about the Velepromet centre?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: Probably, yes, but I cannot -- I have no real memory about that. But we were speaking about some civilians, that they were removed, and so on, and so on. So probably some refugees were mentioned. We have been -- we had been probably offered to go there, so they had to tell us why.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Were you -- sorry. Were you accompanied by a JNA liaison officer throughout this itinerary on the 18th of November as best you can recall?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And when you travelled from OG South headquarters in Negoslavci to Velepromet, did you observe that the Velepromet facility was under JNA control?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Did you meet someone there named Berisavljevic? It's not mentioned in your notes.

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: Berisavljevic. No, I don't remember this.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Do you remember meeting a general or speaking to a General Jerko Crmenic?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: I don't remember. Maybe the sense, yes, but not the names and --

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Do you remember anything about a 5.000th Engineering Unit? And that again is not mentioned in your notes.

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: Yes, this was the -- our report afterwards, I believe 15 days after fall of Vukovar. We were there and then we have been told that -- but I am not quite sure if it is exactly this, but I remember that we were -- we were informed about the asanacion [phoen] of situation, cleaning the city, burying some 100, we were invited to the cemetery and so on. So it was general information what has been done during these 15 days or 14 days.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And were you told that that had been done by this 5.000th Engineering Unit?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: I don't remember. I do remember that there is somewhere written number 5.000, but I don't remember that exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Could we have 00604, please, which is Prosecution tab 4.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And this, sir, is the agreement for the evacuation of the Vukovar Hospital and you've talked about it already. I just want you to have sight, please, of paragraph 5 and it says: "The evacuation will include all those wounded or sick undergoing medical treatment in Vukovar Hospital who are judged by the authorities of the hospital to be fit to make the journey." Now, it's right that this doesn't in terms say that Croatian -- wounded Croatian soldiers are to be included in paragraph 5; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: Sir, I am not a lawyer. As I do understand that it is for me, I can see there the word "all," it means all, whoever it is, whatever rank or civil or military.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Well, I don't necessarily disagree with that interpretation, sir. But what I am interested in is the army's interpretation.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And, if I may, let's please have 005 -- excuse me, 05560, Prosecution tab 32.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Now, am I right, sir, that this is a note of a meeting by Colonel Cunningham at 2.00 on the 19th of November, 1991, and this would have been at the HQ JNA Negoslavci. And you appear to be present; is that right?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: Yes, it is written there that I was there, so definitely.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Under point 1(a) it says: "Whole city, including hospital, under JNA control. Hospital management replaced by JNA military doctors and personnel." Do you remember that you were informed of that during that meeting?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: No, I don't remember that because there were some very different information coming all the time. So I don't remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And if we go over to the next page, we have item 2 -- or, excuse me, subparagraph (d) and this is what it says: "Paragraph 5 of fax signed by Croat and JNA auth evoked much discussion. Colonel Pavkovic stated that POW would not be allowed to depart as: "(1) the POW are under JNA control. "(2) if he did, Serb irregulars/local citizens would attack the convoy. "(3) the POW would be exchanged for JNA POW at some future time." Now, I just want to ask you this precise question: Was Colonel Pavkovic's view that paragraph 5 did not cover these Croatian wounded soldiers?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: I cannot say what was the view of Colonel Pavkovic. What I can say that there was a disagreement between two sides. We were insisting on all and both Cunningham and Dr. Schou and the other side insisted on this -- what is written there. It has been repeated many times during this discussion and this position didn't convert to some common statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Considering what you had observed or were observing in Vukovar in terms of JNA forces, did you have any doubt that the JNA was perfectly capable of providing security for a convoy to evacuate those individuals from the hospital?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: There happened once that one irregular came down to the hospital. On our demand JNA reacted very quickly, removed him. And so it was the only conflict and it was settled in -- very quickly, otherwise I -- JNA in the time we have been there was superior.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And you testified before the Mrksic Chamber when Pavkovic raised this excuse or explanation as to why these wounded soldiers could not be evacuated, namely, the threat from irregulars, you said: We strictly denied it, and we said that we will risk it and we wished to have the convoy as it is, so with all the people.

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Now, I'm right in saying, surely, Mr. Ambassador, that you would never have proposed that if you thought there was any genuine risk to these people; is that right?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: It was told by Cunningham, but we agreed all. For instance, about superiority of JNA, there was a discussion indirectly speaking about the convoy itself. Because there was written that there will be one car of JNA in front and at the end there will be only ECMM mission car and there will not be any guarding car inside of the convoy or at the end of the convoy. This is what I know and this is even what is written in some reports.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Did you know that by this date, namely, the 19th of November, 1991, there already had been a large exchange of Croatian soldiers from Mitnica without that exodus or those soldiers being molested in any way by these irregular forces? Did you know that?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: No, sir, in that time I had no -- I was really concentrated on our task.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Could we please go back to the notebook, and this would be page 7 of the typewritten version. And, Your Honours, I started writing in hand the page numbers --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Excuse me.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: -- and then I recognised that there was a page number at the bottom of the page.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Yes?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: Excuse me. Now I remember that there was an attack on convoy, but it has been convoy of refugees and it is described in one of reports, not of my team, in the coverage of convoys from Vukovar. So there has been some local attack, but not with weapons, if I do remember well.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: That was in Bosnia, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Now, if we go to page 7 of the typewritten version of your diary or your notebook, and this is at 7773, you've got a heading there that says: "Colonel Pavkovic." The notation appears to say "Negoslavci, the 20th of November," and it says: "The wounded men of paramilitary formations should stay here. That is definitely the solution with General Raseta." Now, am I right in thinking that that is information or that is the position being expressed to you by Colonel Pavkovic?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: If it is written there, I don't remember that, but on the other hand, I believe that we still insisted on the written text and if there is a change --

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: I fully understand that, but what I'm very interested in here is on the 19th you're having a disagreement or an agreement with general --

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: And on the 18th as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And on the 18th as well you're having an argument with Colonel Pavkovic and here we are on the morning of the 20th --

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: -- the day of the evacuation itself and two days after you've raised it for the first time. And here we appear to have Colonel Pavkovic sticking to his position, namely, that the wounded soldiers are not to be included in this evacuation. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: So isn't it the case here that really the concern -- and I'm asking for your observation about this. Is it your view that the JNA's concern about a potential threat to the convoy from irregulars was genuine or do you think they were using that as a pretext for their primary position was that Article 5 -- paragraph 5 of the agreement simply did not entitle these wounded soldiers to be evacuated?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: I don't want to guess, so it's more about an analysis than about a real situation. And I cannot confirm that, yes, it was our feeling in this time, but it was not based on anything else than the feeling. On the other hand, I don't think that there is zero risk during the evacuation. There still was some danger, but it can be -- it can be settled by the JNA only to giving more guarding cars into the convoy.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: In other words, it's a risk they could have eliminated; is that right?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Could we have 05113, please, which is Prosecution tab 25.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Now, sir, this is a special report by you, I believe, covering the events of the 20th and the 21st of November in Vukovar.

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And you give there an itinerary or what you call a time schedule. And as I read it, it seems that you -- according to this at least, you're stuck for about two hours, between 8.45 in the morning and 10.45 in the morning, somewhere in Vukovar, but before you're granted access to the hospital; is that right?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: Yes, it is. I already told that it is approximately.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And the reason given to you by the JNA was that there was demining going on; is that right?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Now if we go to page 2 --

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for the Prosecutor, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Sorry, it should be -- it's an under seal document and should not be broadcast.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Thank you. I apologise for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Now, if we go down to point (c) on page 2, we again have a notation which I think means approximately two hours waiting in a centre "(demining?)"?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Do I understand that parenthesis to indicate that your -- and the question mark to indicate skepticism on your part as to whether there really was any demining going on?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: Yes, because we saw that already some JNA cars went there. So I believe that if there is no movement in the neighbourhood there is no so much danger of mines. So it's better to evacuate people as soon as possible. But it's a military decision. I am civilian.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: So do I understand your testimony that you saw JNA vehicles heading along the route towards the Vukovar Hospital from where you were being delayed?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: No, I haven't seen that, but I was told that, yes, there are some vehicles. And when we came there, there were some.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Now, if we can look --

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Please leave the document on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: But now if we could please look at your notebook.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And this is at page 8 of the typewritten version for Your Honours and for the record it's 04687774.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And, sir, perhaps you could just look at it on your binder -- in your binder.

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: Yeah. Can you tell me the number?

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Yes. It is 04687774.

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: I have no such a numbering in my --

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: If I may assist. I believe it is -- did you say 7774?

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Page 16 in e-court, which -- and this is the notebook, correct, is that what you're referring to?

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: The handwritten notebook.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: At tab 34.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: So page?

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: I thank my colleague.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And the part that I'm interested in is: "8.30 colonel spoke with the zone commander for exchange when it comes to JNA road Nustar-Marinci is completely safe. He has no contact with the opposite side. He did not notice any demining from cross-road in direction of Nustar." I just first of all want to ask you: Who is the zone -- do you have any idea who the zone commander for exchange might be?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: No, I have no idea.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And was Colonel Cunningham looking out for demining because both of you were skeptical or suspicious?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: No, I don't think so. We were told: You mustn't go there, so we have to -- it was strict, very strict, what we can do or what not. And this is what you have mentioned on this page. So this is what we have been told. It is nothing of our monitoring.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Now, let's have a look at the document on the screen in front of you, sir. And if we look there at the second paragraph down and it says "briefing by 1," and from page 1 we know that 1 is Colonel Pavkovic, who is noted as the deputy commander of OG south. And here is what the -- here is the information that he appears to be giving you and this is your notation. "The wounded members of Cro paramil forces must stay here (we've been told later by patients that they have been captured and left the hospital before our arr. As well as some people of former personnel Dr. Bosanac ..." So am I right in understanding that the sequence of events here is that you arrive in the centre of Vukovar, you're held up for two hours at this JNA check-point, and it's during those two hours that Croatian -- wounded Croatian soldiers are removed from the hospital?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: I can't say it. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Well, is that what your notes are indicating?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: This is what we have been told.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Did the JNA ever give you any explanation about the removal of those wounded soldiers during the time that you were delayed?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Did you ask them?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: I don't remember. I believe so, but definitely about Dr. Bosanac and Colonel Cunningham settled it.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And am I right that the only institutional authority - and again I use that word "institutional authority" - the only institutional authority with whom you had contact in relation to the evacuation of the Vukovar Hospital, whether it be the 18th, 19th, or 20th, was the JNA?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: Yes, you are right.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Could we have 0 -- well, this is the notebook, but now if we could bring it up on the page or on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And this is page 9 of the typewritten version which is 04687778, sir. It should be the document you've got open right there and if you just move a few more pages along. It's 7778, if you can see --

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: Yes --

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: -- that number?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: -- I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And the notation reads: "Vukovar 11/12," but am I right in believing that it indeed would be the 21st of November that you were making these notes?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: I think that this is the visit afterwards, these 14 days later.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: So you don't think this is the 21st?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: I don't think so because the 20th was the first convoy. The second convoy, I was there in Vukovar only for few hours to load the wounded people and then we went to Bosnia. So I had no time for that. I believe that this date up on the page, 11th of December, is right.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Well, it may not be a major issue, but let's see if there's a reference in here that might help situate us as to the date. If you can turn the page to 7779.

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And you'll see that there there's a reference to: "Still we have small Ustasha groups in cellars." Now, would you agree with me that it's not very likely that there were still Ustasha groups in cellars on the 11th of December, but there probably were still Ustasha groups in cellars on the 21st of November, 1991?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: This is what I was writing there so this is what we were told.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Here we see, whatever the date may be, a reference to Lieutenant-Colonel Vojinovic Milorad comm. Vukovar. And when I say "comm" I mean "comm." And then there's a list: Help inhabitants, keeping order and peace, asanacion of area, demining, cleaning MF, sanction. Am I right --

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: Sanitation, sanitation.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Am I right in understanding that those are the tasks that Lieutenant-Colonel Vojnovic indicated to you were being assumed by the JNA?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And that includes keeping order and peace; correct?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Now, I'd like to ask you some questions about Berak, please.

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And helpfully, there is a reference to your visit there in your notebook and this is on page 12 to 13 of the typewritten version. And this is at 7785 of your handwritten version.

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Now, it says there: Berak 13.12.91. KPT. Mirkovic Colonel Milenkovic changed the structure of the HQ TD, which says Territorial Defence, better relations with JNA. Do I understand this notation to me that these -- well, first of all, let me ask you: Are these JNA officers, Mirkovic and Milenkovic?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: Yes, I believe so.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And do I understand that what this notation is describing that they, namely Mirkovic and Milenkovic, have changed the structure of the TO HQ, whatever that might be, but that that's what they've done?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: As I do remember, Territorial Defence was a standard part of Yugoslav army, so, yes, there were some reservists but it was an organic part. So these -- this captain and colonel were standard JNA officers.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And they were exercising command authority over --

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: This is what we have been told.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And were they the ones who told you that, Milinkovic and Mirkovic, if you can recall? You may not be able to recall, but can you recall that?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: I am not able. Maybe they were presented by liaison officer like -- I don't really remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And then your next notation is: "Chance to go to home or to choose the place to go. Safety inhabitants is guaranteed. If we find guilty of some people they will be judged by the law." Do I understand that essentially they are describing their policy --

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: -- in respect of Croatian civilians who are still living in the area?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Could we have 06110, which is Defence tab 69. And I believe that this one is probably under seal and should not be broadcast.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Now, sir, I'm not saying that you've seen this report, but we see up there in the top left-hand corner that it's dated the 26th of February, possibly 1992. And if we just go down to the very last page, which is page 4, and the document, for the record, is to the 1st Motorised Corps command. And down at the end it says: "Authorised by the commander Lieutenant-Colonel Petar Mirkovic." Is there any possibility that this is the same individual whom you refer to in your notes as Captain Mirkovic?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: Sir, I cannot guess.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Let's turn back, please, to page 2, and there is a reference here to Berak and that's why I'm showing you this document. And in the lead-up to that reference is as follows. "What all local communes in the zone of responsibility of the brigade have in common is that they are disturbed by the security and political situation in Boksic village. "The situation in Tompojevci village is somewhat less dramatic as the local commune Executive Council has been organised as one organ, which is in contradiction with the principles of organisation and functioning of the authorities. In addition to this, a TO platoon could not be formed as ordered and regulated by the 1st Motorised Corps command strictly confidential number 397/II-2 of 16 February 1992 which was reported by this command in a timely fashion as requested. "In Sremski Cakovci (excluding Boksic village), the local commune executive councils and the TO staff of the villages of Berak and Miklusevci have split up their jurisdictions and duties which means that the authorities are functioning ..." Now, is this consistent with your understanding that the JNA is taking control of organising or reorganising TO forces in this area?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: As I told you what I do know is that Territorial Defence was a part of these defence structures. On the other hand, in Yugoslavia it was very connected or linked together, the leadership or crisis leadership, let's say. So I have no idea about these responsibilities of one or the other person. What I can say as an analysis that if Supreme Command headquarters in Belgrade, they know what has happened in Berak, that there is some isolation camp, they can settle the situation before they permit us to go there. So if they allow that, I believe that at least the headquarters they have no idea about this.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: But you can't exclude -- in fact, wouldn't it be highly -- hard to understand that these senior JNA officials on the ground wouldn't be aware of what you describe as a detention site containing 50 elderly Croat civilians?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: Yes, I was speaking about headquarters in Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Can we go back, please, to your --

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: But, if you allow me, sir, these detainees were guarded by a civilian person or volunteer of course with weapon but partly in civil clothes. He was the young guy. I remember that my Dutch colleague offered him a cigarette and he said: No, no, no, I cannot smoke because my wife -- my mother prohibited it. So this is what I do remember as a moment from -- he was guarding these people.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Well, did you ever see TO soldiers who weren't wearing regular uniforms?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: Some of them, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Those were precisely the people who were under the command of the JNA; correct?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Now, sir, if I turn you to your notebook again in respect of Berak - and we'll have to go back, please, on the screen to 05673 - and, sir, for your reference again that's 7783.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: For Your Honours, that's page 12 to 13 of the typewritten version.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Now, you've testified here today about a detention site containing 50 --

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: Around.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: -- Croatian soldiers -- Croatian civilians between the ages of 55 and 88 years old, I believe.

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Must have been quite a remarkable and disturbing sight?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And can you explain why this is not mentioned in your notebook?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: It was not necessary. I do remember it well and you can see detailed I mentioned to you so ...

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: But wouldn't this event been something that you should have reported up the chain of your own reporting channels?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: I don't have a copy. Probably there is some report in the mission where Berak was covered on, but I have no copy of that. So these are only my remarks, and I am not marking, I am not writing what I do remember well. So I am writing more -- I have no time to write everything, so ...

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Isn't it true that when we look at all of the reports that you had anything to do with, that there's no or virtually no mention at all of the district government in the area?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: Yes, because we were in a contact with JNA and we were provided by the JNA liaison officers interpreters.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And there's no mention at all of any contact with Mr. Hadzic, is there?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: I don't remember that. I do remember that once we were invited for some discussion to Erdut, but then it has been -- or cancelled or something like that. But I have no real memory about any contact in this sense.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: As far as you're concerned at least in the area of OG South, the areas that you were visiting, the district government had no presence at all; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: I can't say it 100 per cent. I'm not sure if in Velepromet there were no some people from the municipality or from the civil part of civil authorities. But I'm not denying, neither confirming. But we were speaking there with people in civil clothes so it's obvious.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: During your testimony in Mrksic you said and you were asked: "Well, let's see if we can try and remember where you are when this was being said to you." And I believe this is -- concerns the 19th of November in Vukovar --

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Excuse me, sorry. I would be assisted by a page reference.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And the question -- well, let's go back, let's do both questions that you were asked. "Now, who was telling you that the volunteers would not allow the convoy to pass through, and indeed if there was a single Croatian soldier/Ustasha on it? "A. I don't remember. It was somebody from JNA side."

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: "Q. Well, let's see if we can try and remember where you are when this was being said to you. Now, who was telling you this? Was it military or was it civilian? "Answer" -- and this is your answer: "No, military. They were on the other side from the side of JNA, there were only -- only military persons. I don't remember that there are some civilians."

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: Yes, it was about negotiation in Negoslavci. What I am mentioning now, that there is only a slight possibility that in the Velepromet we were speaking with people in civil clothes. I cannot say more. I do remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: But you can't confirm whether any of these people had anything to do with the district government of the SBWS?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: No, no. No idea. No idea and no remarks in my textbook.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Ambassador, for your answers.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Mr. President, thank you, those are my questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Ms. Biersay, do you have questions for re-direct?

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: I do not, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: You do not. Mr. Ambassador, this brings your testimony to an end. We thank you very much for coming to The Hague to assist the Tribunal. You're now released as a witness. The court usher will escort you out of court and we wish you a safe journey home. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Gosnell.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Sorry, Mr. President, I believe I neglected to tender 65 ter 06110 which I would propose now to tender, if I may. It's Defence tab 69.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: No objections, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Shall be assigned D36, admitted under seal, if I'm correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Yeah, that's correct. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Anything else?

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Not on my behalf, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: So we adjourn for the week --

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Just for the record one correction. It should be admitted as D37, not 36. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. So we adjourn for the week and we resume on Monday morning at 9.00 -- no, on Tuesday morning, 9.00. Court adjourned.
